item.text: {"text":"Recent evidence separates useful history from complex sequence modeling. A [RecSys 2026 study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) reports that recency-weighted pairwise transition models outperform SASRec/eSASRec reproductions on four of five benchmarks; older interactions help even without joint contextualization. These results concern different datasets and protocols from the specified RecHarness task. [Liu et al., RecSys 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042) show that arbitrary history shuffling conflates behavioral order with item availability; their constrained shuffling prevents interactions from preceding an item’s first observed appearance. [Robust Training, 2024](https://iris.uniroma1.it/bitstream/11573/1740238/1/Siciliano_Robust-Training_2024.pdf) specifically investigates missing recent interactions and robustness-oriented training.\n\nSuggested diagnostic synthesis: pair each recent-interaction deletion with equal-count deletions elsewhere in the same history; separately remove repeated or isolated interactions, matching controls on training-item popularity where feasible. Compare full shuffling with shuffling that preserves the last item, keeping the item multiset fixed; availability-constrained variants provide another control. Hold validation targets and candidate sets constant. Measure paired target-rank changes, HR@10 differences, and recommendation overlap; report per-category effects and user-bootstrap confidence intervals for the macro-average. Repeat randomized controls to quantify perturbation variability. Larger recent-deletion effects than matched controls suggest predictive reliance on recent evidence; ranking churn without accuracy loss suggests sensitivity without demonstrated usefulness. These probes measure model behavior under edited inputs, not causal effects on user preferences. Connections to positional encoding, attention, or training loss remain hypotheses until controlled model ablations support them."}
